messages:
maria-dev: Heads-up — ran a focused fp16 latency/throughput microbench for the same A100 SKU across AWS, GCP, and Azure using our inference container (redwood/infer:v2). Results look off.
sam-ml: curious — what metric is off? p50/p95 or steady throughput?
maria-dev: p95 and tail jitter for short-context (seq=128) generation. Numbers:

    AWS us-east-1 (a100-80gb, driver 525.85, CUDA 11.8): p95=48ms, p99=82ms, throughput=210 tokens/s
    GCP us-central1 (a100-80gb, driver 535.113, CUDA 12.1): p95=64ms, p99=115ms, throughput=195 tokens/s
    Azure westeurope (a100-80gb, driver 525.85, CUDA 11.8): p95=60ms, p99=108ms, throughput=198 tokens/s

maria-dev: note — image, model binary, and run flags identical. test script: `bench/run_micro_infer.sh --model t5x-small --seq 128 --batch 1 --dtype fp16 --iters 2000`

devon-infra: did you warm up long enough? fp16 kernels sometimes have a warmup path for cuBLAS/cutlass JIT that stabilizes after ~500 iters.
maria-dev: warmed with 500 iters as part of run, but I separately tried 2k warmup and still saw GCP 20-30% higher p95 vs AWS for the same steady-state window.

lee-sre: any difference in clock/power governor or firmware? GCP sometimes ships a slightly different GPU firmware or BIOS tuning that keeps clocks aggressive only after sustained load.

maria-dev: looked at `nvidia-smi` during runs:

    # AWS
    Driver Version: 525.85.12
    GPU Temp: 64C
    Power Draw: 250W
    Clocks: SM 1410 MHz

    # GCP
    Driver Version: 535.113.02
    GPU Temp: 58C
    Power Draw: 200W
    Clocks: SM 1080 MHz (saw stepping during request bursts)

maria-dev: also saw higher PCIe latency samples on GCP region.

nora-eng: do you have kernel logs or dmesg? sometimes kernel versions interact with NV drivers (iommu, p2p). what OS images?
maria-dev: AWS AMI: ubuntu-20.04 + kernel 5.15. GCP image: cos-99 + kernel 5.15 (container-optimized), Azure: Ubuntu 20.04 + kernel 5.15. So kernel looks similar; driver differs for GCP.

sam-ml: could be cuBLAS/cutlass autotune producing a different kernel selection — driver+CUDA 12.1 picks new kernels that are slower for our sequence length/shape. Have you captured kernel names (nvprof / nsight)?

maria-dev: ran `nvprof --print-gpu-trace` quick capture. On AWS we get `cutlass_gemm_fp16_sm80` as dominant, on GCP I saw `fmha_forward_fp16_sm80_variantB` for some steps.

devon-infra: that smells like a kernel selection difference. If cuBLAS/attention autotune picks an fmha variant on GCP that has worse latency for short sequences, that explains p95 regression but not throughput collapse.

lee-sre: try forcing the kernel selection or pinning CUDA flags. For a quick test, set `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` or `TF_CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG`? Also try `--cutlass-autotune=false` if our binary supports it.

maria-dev: good idea. I ran a controlled switch by downgrading driver+CUDA in a GCP VM to 11.8 + driver 525.85 (same as AWS) — p95 dropped to ~50ms. Means driver+CUDA combo drives it.

nora-eng: did you also check MIG partitions? if VM had multitenant noisy neighbor, could affect clocks. but seems driver is main suspect.

maria-dev: verified MIG disabled, single tenant. Also tried PCIe gen negotiation forced to 3.0 on GCP host (no change).

sam-ml: important note for model onboarding checklist: add a quick kernel-hash capture and driver/CUDA fingerprint. We'll need to record `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,firmware_version --format=csv` and `nvcc --version` and a small `nvprof` capture.

bench-bot: automated artifact: uploaded microbench traces -> s3://redwood-bench/artifacts/2123456789/fp16-gcp-nvprof.log

maria-dev: follow-ups:
- file an infra ticket to request GCP instances with driver 525.85 image for parity tests
- add a pre-onboarding checklist step to run 2000-iter warmup + kernel sampling for new regions
- add a regression alert comparing p95 vs baseline across providers

devon-infra: I'll spin a GCP VM with 525.85/CUDA11.8 and try to reproduce with our cluster image.

lee-sre: also add a perf regression knob in console: if p95 jumps >15% vs baseline for a pinned model+SKU, warn and suggest fallback to a different CUDA path.

nora-eng: capturing for docs: short writeup with commands and the nvprof snippet would be helpful. I'll paste the minimal repro in the onboarding playbook.

maria-dev: thanks — creating a short PR with the checklist and linking the nvprof output.

sam-ml: good catch. this is a nice reminder that same SKU != same runtime behavior.

maria-dev: exact. logging the ticket: #INFRA-1427 (investigate GCP A100 driver/kernel selection mismatch)

lee-sre: ping me if you want a hand with firmware / BIOS parity checks.

maria-dev: will do. end of thread.
